clips.title: The story
paras: You carry Laird's findings from Auberdine back to Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. The journey is an introductory errand that teaches young travelers how to cross between Kalimdor and Teldrassil.

Laird sends you back across the water with his written observations. He has found stark differences between the fish caught off Darkshore and those near Teldrassil, and suspects the great World Tree changes the local marine life. You can return to Rut'theran Village by hiring a flight from Caylais Moonfeather, the hippogryph master, or by boarding the regular ferry at Auberdine's pier.

Nessa Shadowsong receives Laird's reply at Rut'theran Village and is fascinated by the difference in marine life. Fish near the World Tree grow so large that they bring an immediate boon to local fishermen, though the Kaldorei still do not know why. Nessa plans to share the findings with her fellow villagers. For now, she is content to harvest the abundant sea life and watch for whatever forces may be responsible.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: I must send a response to Nessa. She'll be very interested to know how different the fish here are from those along Teldrassil's coastline. We can only guess the cause, but it is my suspicion that the world tree itself is affecting the wildlife around it!

Please, take this response to Nessa. If you wish to take a hippogryph back to Rut'theran then speak with the hippogryph master Caylais Moonfeather. If you wish to take the ferry, then one regularly departs from the dock to the northwest.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Friend, you're back from Auberdine? Did you speak with Laird?

clips.title: Completion
paras: This is very interesting. The fish here are large, but I didn't think the difference in bounties between here and the mainland was so great. There must be a reason for this...
Well thank you, friend. I will discuss with the villagers the news you brought. Perhaps, one day, we will find the root of this oddity. But until then, we shall reap its benefits!
